_meta.basis: Consolidated, Rs crore unless stated. Every fact has a source (src) and its publication date (published); nothing published after 30-Sep-2026 is used here (later facts: updates/later-facts.json).

profile.what: Biocon is a Bengaluru-based biopharmaceutical group with three businesses: biosimilars (Biocon Biologics, BBL: copies of biologic drugs such as insulins and cancer and immunology antibodies; 61% of FY26 revenue), generics (APIs and finished generics, incl. GLP-1 peptides; 17%) and research services (Syngene International, a listed contract research and manufacturing company, 52.4% owned; 22%). It also holds 5.52 mn shares (~10%) of Bicara Therapeutics (Nasdaq: BCAX), a US cancer-drug developer it incubated.
profile.scale: 12 biosimilars commercialised, 20+ in the pipeline; 30+ generic formulations; >120 countries; 7 manufacturing sites, 3 R&D sites, 9,500+ employees (Q1FY27 press release).

structure.bbl: Biocon Biologics (biosimilars): 76.8% owned at Mar-25, 98.7% at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 39), 99.2% at 1-Jun-2026 (June-2026 investor presentation), wholly owned from 29-Jun-2026 after 8.79 mn Biocon shares were issued at Rs376.41 for the last 0.8% (MOSL 6-Aug-2026; SHP Jun-2026). Integration completed in under 100 days; 'OneBiocon' from 1-Apr-2026 (Q4FY26 call; AR FY26 Board's report).

steps.what: BBL completes the acquisition of Viatris's biosimilars business for up to $3.335 bn ($2.335 bn cash + $1 bn of BBL preference shares to Viatris); ~$1.2 bn of acquisition debt.
BBL refinances the acquisition loans with $800 mn of 6.67% senior secured notes (5-year, non-call 2) and a $320 mn syndicated loan; Rs121.6 cr of unamortised costs written off (AR FY26 note 32i).

QIP: 13.64 cr shares at Rs330 (Rs4,500 cr) to redeem structured instruments: Goldman Sachs OCDs of BBL (Rs1,125 cr, Jun-25), Kotak NCDs (Rs1,070 cr, 1-Oct-25), Edelweiss NCDs (Rs500 cr) and CCDs (Rs300 cr, 5-Jan-26). Saves ~Rs300 cr of interest a year.
steps.src: AR FY26 Secretarial audit report and Board's report

steps.what: Board approves full integration of BBL: buy Viatris's stake for $815 mn ($400 mn cash + $415 mn in Biocon shares at 61.70 Biocon shares per 100 BBL shares) and swap Serum Institute Life Sciences, Tata Capital Growth Fund II and Activ Pine into Biocon shares (70.28 per 100); BBL valued at $5.5 bn at Rs405.78 a Biocon share. Merger and IPO were considered and rejected.
17.13 cr Biocon shares issued to Mylan (Viatris), Serum, Tata Capital and Activ Pine for 26.19 cr BBL shares; Mylan paid $200 mn on 5-Jan and $200 mn on 21-Jan for 14.37 cr BBL shares.
QIP: 11.27 cr shares at Rs368.35 (Rs4,150 cr) to fund the Viatris cash payment; SBI MF and ICICI Prudential MF took ~29.5% each.
Last 0.8% of BBL acquired by issuing 8,786,362 shares (Rs376.41); BBL wholly owned; 162.97 cr shares outstanding.

syngene.src: AR FY26 note 39 (52.5% at Mar-25; 54.9% at Mar-24; 70.4% at Mar-22 per Screener)

bicara.note: Quoted at fair value through OCI (AR FY26 note 5); 9.8% stake per the June-2026 investor presentation (10.1% in the AR). Bicara's founding CEO is Claire Mazumdar, the chairperson's niece; Bicara is a related party. Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw on 6-Aug-2026: 'no longer a significant investment', will monetise 'at the right time'.

fy25.src: AR FY26 note 22 and 40; Q4FY26 presentation p.8, p.12

points: Biosimilars EBITDA Rs728 cr, 25% margin; R&D 7% of revenue; 'meaningful acceleration in the second half of FY27'.
Second drug-product line at the Malaysia insulin plant approved by the EMA; supplies started, picking up from Q2FY27; Malaysia drug-substance doubling by end-FY27 (Q4 call).

Yesafili (aflibercept) launched in the US in August as an interchangeable biosimilar; Bosaya/Aukelso (denosumab) ramping; glargine share rising; Kirsty (aspart) moving from closed-door networks to commercial players.
Five focus products: aflibercept, denosumab, aspart, ustekinumab, bevacizumab; July-September is the US payer contracting window.
CFO: normalise FY26's 27% biosimilars margin to ~24-25%; management guides to 'mid-20s, will ramp up'. 'Price erosion is real.'
Generics EBITDA Rs56 cr (7%), up >250bp QoQ on API pricing premiums, R&D pruning and opex cuts; API:formulations ~60:40; liraglutide 'in single digits' of the segment.

Syngene: revenue -16% on lower offtake from a key biologics client and a forex hedge loss; FY27 a 'transition year', single-digit rupee decline, return to growth from FY28. Siddharth Mittal now Syngene CEO.
Net debt up ~Rs1,100 cr QoQ on inventory for the second-half launches; every dollar of free cash to debt reduction; biosimilars inventory days normalised to 280-290 from 400+.
US tariffs: generics and biosimilars exempt under current law; the President's tariff post 'just a tweet'; no new US capex, partnerships instead.
Bicara 'no longer a significant investment', will monetise 'at the right time'.
Net debt incl. structured instruments >$1.5 bn at Mar-25, $1.1 bn at Mar-26; will hover at $1.1-1.2 bn subject to working capital; interest down from ~Rs280-300 cr a quarter to ~Rs210-220 cr.
Insulin franchise >$300 mn a year; adalimumab >$250 mn; pegfilgrastim and trastuzumab ~$200 mn; bevacizumab >$100 mn (before the US launch).
US oncology biosimilar shares steady at 23-25%; glargine ~11%; ustekinumab close to a fifth of the US biosimilar market (IQVIA, Feb-26).
Biosimilars split ~40% North America, ~35% Europe (incl. Japan, ANZ), ~25% emerging markets; North America ~46% in Q4.
Generics gross margin early 40s; API two-thirds; GLP-1 <10% of the segment in FY26; no large greenfield capex needed.
$800 mn 6.67% notes callable from Oct-2026 at a premium; both rating agencies upgraded; no hedging of the dollar debt (natural hedge).
FDA's draft guidance waiving phase-3 studies halves biosimilar development cost and cuts 3-4 years; higher analytical bar favours incumbents (CEO).

guidance.fy27: Growth accelerating through the year, stronger second half; biosimilars EBITDA margin 'mid-20s' and rising; generics margin expansion; Syngene single-digit rupee decline with margins recovering; capex lower; free cash to debt reduction (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls). MOSL reads the consolidated EBITDA margin guidance as ~24-25% (company basis).

generics.what: 79 APIs and 83 formulations (22 launched in the US) per Screener key points; API ~60-67% of the segment (statins, immunosuppressants such as tacrolimus, fermentation-based peptides); formulations in the US (Cranbury NJ oral solids), Europe and emerging markets. GLP-1: first generic liraglutide approval in a regulated market (UK, 2024); US approvals for gVictoza and gSaxenda in Q4FY26, US launch Q1FY27; EU and Australia approvals. New capacity at Vizag and Hyderabad (API), Bengaluru (peptides, injectables) and Cranbury (phase 2).

points: Promoters 44.68% after three equity raises and the BBL share swap (60.64% at Mar-25); nothing pledged except Ravi Mazumdar's 0.33% (encumbered).
Independent directors Bobby Parikh (term ended 22-Jul-2026) and Nicholas Haggar (until the 6-Aug-2026 AGM) leaving.
Succession: founder-chair, no children; niece Claire Mazumdar (Bicara CEO) named eventual chair; operating leadership professional (Tambe, Upadhye).
Related party: Bicara (a director sits on its board); Biocon holds ~10%.

June-2022: CBI arrested a BBL associate vice-president and a Joint Drugs Controller in an alleged bribery case over waiving a phase-3 trial for insulin aspart in India; the company denied wrongdoing; no outcome found by 30-Sep-2026.
Credit: CRISIL AA+/Stable and ICRA AA+/Stable reaffirmed Dec-2025; S&P and Fitch upgrades in FY26 (AR FY26).
Auditor B S R & Co. (KPMG network); FY26 had Rs403 cr of exceptional items and Rs400 cr+ of 'non-recurring' costs, the sixth year in a row with exceptional items.
